# Case 31: Hypothesis Testing

## Introduction

This report examines two hypotheses concerning members’ awareness of Credit Union services and their opinions about Credit Union loan rates. A one-way ANOVA was used for H1, and a paired-samples t-test was used for H2.

# Hypothesis 1 (H1)

## Awareness of Regular Share Accounts and Service Satisfaction

H1 examines whether members’ awareness of regular share accounts is related to their opinions about how well the Credit Union’s financial services meet their needs.

- Predictor: Q13, awareness of regular share accounts
- Outcome: Q33, whether the Credit Union’s financial services meet members’ needs

Q13 contains three awareness groups:

1. Aware and have used the service
2. Aware but have not used the service
3. Unaware of the service

# Hypothesis 2 (H2)

## Credit Union Loan Rates and Competitor Comparisons

H2 examines whether members’ opinions of the Credit Union’s loan rates differ from their agreement that the Credit Union’s loan rates are lower than those of competitors.

The two ratings were measured using:

- Q8: Opinion about rates charged on borrowed funds
- Q30: Agreement that Credit Union loan rates are lower than other institutions

Because the same respondents answered both questions, a paired-samples t-test was appropriate.
